messages:
sara: Heads-up — we need to decide how Dedicated enforces reserved throughput vs bursts. Current ask from infra: tenants should get their committed RPS, but idle capacity should be usable by other tenants for short bursts. How strict should isolation be?
ben: Short answer: soft isolation with a fair-burst policy. Let unused reserved capacity be borrowable but enforce a global upper bound so a single noisy tenant can't OOM the pool.
kai: Agree with soft isolation, but implementation matters. Do we police at the gateway (edge) or on the GPU worker? Token-bucket at gateway => simple, but inaccurate when requests queue on workers. Worker-side enforcement can account for actual concurrent resource usage.
elena: We also need to show this in Console. Proposal: two metrics per tenant: "reserved_utilization" and "burst_consumption", plus a forecast for when burst will be throttled. UX should show a single gauge with stacked colors (reserved + burst).
michael: Ops concern: if we allow burst across tenants in the same dedicated pool, we must emit explicit telemetry events so SRE can alert on aggregate burst over X%. Events: quota.burst_granted, quota.burst_denied, quota.reserve_reclaimed.
opsbot: Deploy-check: quota.enforcement_mode currently defaults to "monitor" in staging. Canary flag available: quota.mode=soft-enforce.
sara: Implementation idea I sketched: keep per-tenant token-bucket for reserved RPS (refill rate = reserved_rps), and a shared burst pool token-bucket for the pool. When tenant consumes > reserved, pull from shared pool. If shared pool empty => tenant gets soft-throttled (HTTP 429 with Retry-After).
ben: That works. Two follow-ups: 1) fairness: cap per-tenant burst share so a huge tenant can't drain shared pool instantly, 2) leak-proofing: if a tenant is misbehaving, ability to pin-limit it quickly.
kai: Fairness cap example: max_burst_per_tenant = min( shared_pool * 0.25, reserved_rps * 4 ). Means a single tenant can use up to 25% of pool or 4x its reserved, whichever is smaller.
elena: Console config UI needs a toggle for "Allow soft burst" and a slider for "max tenant burst multiplier". Also expose audit log entries when a tenant consumes > reserved (so customer success can explain billing/behavior).
michael: Telemetry JSON we should emit (example):
```json
{
  "event": "quota.burst_granted",
  "tenant_id": "org_123",
  "pool_id": "dedicated-eu-west-1-a",
  "granted_tokens": 1200,
  "timestamp": 1769051234
}
```
We just need fields consistent across events. Use human-readable metric names for dashboards.
alice: Rollout plan suggestion: 1) monitor mode for 2 weeks (collect burst metrics) 2) enable soft-enforce for 10% of pools (low-risk tenants) for 1 week 3) expand to 50% with canary dashboards 4) hard-enforce only after 4 weeks of stable metrics.
sara: Edge vs worker enforcement: leaning worker-side enforcement + gateway hinting. Gateway checks quick token bucket and tags request with consumed_tokens header. Worker does final accounting and may reclaim if overconsumed. That avoids double-counting when retries happen.
kai: We must handle retries/backoff loops: include a retry_budget header so clients with exponential backoff don't keep consuming burst. Also emit metric retry_budget_exhausted.
elben: (typo) — sorry, meant elena: One more UX thought: in per-tenant quota page, show a small timeline of recent throttle events and the top endpoints that caused bursts (so customers can optimize prompts).
ben: We should also plan for billing implications — if burst is free up to X, fine. If we bill bursts at premium, Console needs to expose projected cost increase when burst is consumed. Add burst_cost_rate to telemetry.
michael: Ops-wise, add an alert: If pool-level burst consumption > 60% for > 5m, page SRE. Also a soft alert at 30% for product to review.
sara: Ok action items: @ben to write ticket for policy alg + config knobs, @kai to prototype worker enforcement and header contract, @elena for Console mockups + telemetry names, @michael for SLO/alert thresholds and event schema. I'll run rollout calendar draft after tickets land.
ben: I'll open the RFC with a sample config snippet: 
```yaml
quota_policy:
  reserved_rps: 200
  allow_soft_burst: true
  max_burst_multiplier: 4
  max_burst_share_of_pool: 0.25
  enforcement_point: worker
  enforcement_mode: monitor #|soft-enforce|hard-enforce
```

kai: Nits: rename max_burst_share_of_pool -> max_pool_share_per_tenant for clarity.
elena: Also add ui_labels for telemetry mapping: reserved -> "Reserved throughput", burst -> "Burst".
opsbot: Note: created incident simulation job to validate throttling behavior in chaos stage. job id ci-5489.
sara: Great, thanks. Let's reconvene after the RFC + prototype. :thumbsup:
